key_insight: PyroDash teaches a small language model to trigger token-level handoffs to a frozen large model only when needed, cutting inference cost while preserving strong mathematical reasoning accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This enables cheaper, scalable serving for reasoning systems by internalizing routing inside the SLM and avoiding separate routers, LLM retraining, or access to LLM logits.
method: Learns a control token that lets the SLM request LLM assistance mid-generation.
Uses a single handoff Collaborate Engine to pass the query plus partial reasoning trace to the frozen LLM.
Trains in three stages: control-token embedding learning, offloading-focused SFT, and cost-aware GRPO alignment.
evidence_signal: On five math reasoning benchmarks, PyroDash achieved different accuracy-cost tradeoffs, including 64.04% average accuracy at λ=0.05 with 20.4% cost reduction, and 54.55% accuracy at λ=0.6 with only 0.012 LLM calls per example.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful reward tuning and benchmark-specific behavior, so real-world gains may vary with prompt complexity, model choice, and cost accounting assumptions.
paper_title: PyroDash: Cost-Efficient Token-Level Small-Large Language Model Collaborative Inference
